title: Artery Embolization Versus Nerve Cryoablation for Knee Osteoarthritis
official: Genicular Artery Embolization Versus Genicular Nerve Cryoablation for Symptomatic Knee Osteoarthritis
summary: This study will compare two procedures for knee pain caused by osteoarthritis. One procedure blocks small arteries supplying the painful area of the knee. The other uses cold to treat nerves that carry pain signals from the knee. Each eligible knee will be assigned by chance to one of the procedures. The main question is how much pain, stiffness, and difficulty with daily activities improve six months after the first technically successful procedure. Participants will also report knee symptoms and function at three and twelve months. If symptoms improve by less than the study threshold at six months, the study team will offer the other procedure when clinically appropriate.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults with at least three months of persistent knee pain primarily attributable to radiographically documented osteoarthritis despite appropriate conservative care, or with documented intolerance or a contraindication to such care.
* Participants must be able to give informed consent, report outcomes separately for each study knee, and accept random assignment.
* Prior intra-articular injections and nonprocedural care are permitted. Enrollment will be deferred if a recent injection or changing symptoms would make baseline scores unstable.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior surgery, arthroplasty, arthroscopy, embolization, therapeutic nerve intervention, or another invasive treatment of the study knee other than intra-articular injection. A diagnostic local anesthetic block is permitted.
* Planned knee replacement before the six-month assessment, active infection, acute fracture, or a different primary cause of pain such as inflammatory arthritis or radiculopathy.
* Unsafe arterial access or perfusion, dependence on genicular collateral vessels, unacceptable contrast or bleeding risk, or a contraindication to either procedure or to imipenem-cilastatin.
